summary: Kamal K. Sridhar is a scholar in linguistics and Indology. She served at Stony Brook University as director, attested in 2007, and later as Professor Emerita, attested in 2026.

Kamala Tiyavanich works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. She studied at Cornell University under David K. Wyatt, A. Thomas Kirsch, and Richard Polenberg, and held a Mellon Postdoctoral Fellowship there from 1993 to 1994.

Kamaleswar Bhattacharya (1928–2014) was a scholar in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at the University of Toronto (~1967–1969), Brown University (~1970–1972), and the University of Bonn.

Kameshwar Nath Mishra works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He was a professor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1982–1988, 2001) and served as a Visiting Research Scholar at the University of Marburg in 1993.

Kamil Václav Zvelebil (1927–2009) was a linguist and Indologist who earned his PhD from Charles University in 1952. He held appointments at the Oriental Institute (1952–1970), Charles University (~1952–1968), and Utrecht University (~1978–1992).

Kamla Chowdhry (1920–2006) studied at Santiniketan, the University of the Punjab, the University of Calcutta (~1941–1943), and Michigan State University (~1946–1949). She held posts at the Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (~1962–1972) and Harvard University.

Kamlesh Dutt Tripathi is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied under Kshetresh Chandra Chattopadhyaya. He served as professor emeritus at Banaras Hindu University, Chairman of the Kalidasa Sanskrit Academy, and Advisor at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts.

Kammie Takahashi is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Mount Holyoke College and earned a PhD from the University of Virginia (~2002–2009) under David Germano and Paul Groner. She held a post at Muhlenberg College in 2011.
Kan Hang (born 1965) is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Su Bai and served as Dean of the School of Archaeology and Museology at Peking University.

Kanai Lal Hazra (born 1932) is a Buddhist studies and history scholar who completed a PhD at the University of Ceylon in 1968 under Sirima Kiribamune. He served as a Lecturer in Pali at the University of Calcutta, attested in 1982.
Kanchu Onoue is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He held posts as an instructor at Hikone Higashi High School, attested in 1963, and as a professor at Eizan Gakuin, attested in 1976.

Kang-nam Oh is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies who completed a doctorate under Yün-hua Jan and studied at the University of Tokyo (1973–1974). He held an academic post at the University of Regina, attested 1990–1998.

Kang-yuan Sung is a scholar of religious studies and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA at the University of Calgary, where he was supervised by Anthony W. Barber and taught by Anne Moore and Leslie S. Kawamura.

Kangei Okamoto (1899–1948) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied under Takamatsu Yoshie, attended the University of Paris, and worked as an appointee at Tokyo National Museum.

Kanji Tamura (born 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. His career includes appointments at Rissho University, where he was attested as a part-time lecturer in the Faculty of Buddhist Studies in 2001 and as an associate professor in 2026.
Kanoko Tanaka is a scholar in religious studies and Indology who studied under Acharya Tulsi. She served as a part-time lecturer in religious studies at Komazawa University, attested in 2001.
Kansei Tamura (1928–2018) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo, attested in 1962. He also served as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1962.
Kanti Chandra Pandey (1903–1971) was a scholar in Indology and philosophy who founded the University of Lucknow, where he also held a post attested in 1950.

Kapila Vatsyayan (1928–2020) was an Indology and history scholar educated at Delhi, Michigan, and Banaras Hindu University. She taught at Delhi and BHU, founded the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts, and served as chairperson of the India International Centre.

Karam Tej Singh Sarao (born 1955) is an Indologist and historian. He earned degrees at Delhi and a PhD at Cambridge (1985–1989) under Frank Raymond Allchin and K. R. Norman, later serving as professor at the University of Delhi from 1995.
